newspec-c: record-only → passed (record only (every judged cell passed, the rest is recorded only))
Our own boundary case (2026-10-15 review: record-only). PW, local stack. Device A's clock started at Oct 14 23:57 JST (behind the real clock); at 23:59 P1 (Hospital) and R1 (Nursing Home) were set to New Admission on their charts (stored new@2026-10-14); the Hospital and Nursing Home lists stayed open in two tabs while the clock ran past midnight; at 00:01 P2 / R2 were set to Consult (stored consult@2026-10-15); P3 / R3 carried a future-stamped day 2026-10-16 (what a device a day ahead stores on main). Seen: at 00:00:38, no reload, the open lists already read Follow-up for P1 / R1 (client-side render; the server still had new@2026-10-14), and by the 10-minute lifecycle repeat the roll was stored (follow-up@2026-10-15); P2 / R2 stayed Consult that day; device B on the real clock showed the same badges as A. 'Next midnight' emulated by moving every stored day back one day: P2 / R2 rolled to Follow-up, but P3 / R3 still read New Admission and rolled only a day later - the device-clock day stored by a fast device (known B18, TFA-92584 AC 8). Q1 (recorded): the roll follows the physician's local midnight (00:00 JST), not server UTC midnight (09:00 JST).

Approach · TC-06 Admission Status Toggle · S10 Midnight edges on the server clock: set at 23:59, set at 00:01, a future-stamped day, list left open across midnight

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U5 New Admission and Consult both roll to Follow-up on the next calendar day without the physician touching them; a status set today stays today (UAT TC-06; TFA-92584 AC 4)
  • U6 The day roll uses server time, not the device clock: a device with a wrong date, no clock set or another time zone shows the same badge and the same pre-selected template as any other device, and nev … (UAT TC-06; UAT 3.8; TFA-92584 AC 8)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given Hospital patient and resident; physician sets New Admission at 23:59 and Consult at 00:01 (server day, Q1 time zone); one row stamped encTypeDay = server day + 1 (what a device whose clock is ahead writes on main)

When Move the server clock to 00:00:30 and to 23:59 of the same day, then past the next midnight; keep one list open across midnight and re-open the other

Then 23:59 status reads Follow-up from 00:00 on; 00:01 status stays all day and rolls at the next midnight; the future-stamped row reads Follow-up from the next server midnight, not a day later; the open list updates without a reload; every device agrees

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT TC-06 + 3.8. Which midnight counts is Q1; the list update delay is not specified (lifecycle re-runs every 10 min). Day roll on the device clock is known: TFA-92584 AC 8

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method TIME · Time / aging (clock moved); lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (blocked)

S10 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-06.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: TIME · Time / aging (clock moved); secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local (23:59/00:01 and list-open-across-midnight cells) / dev (future-stamped encTypeDay cell through seed and applyLifecycle); Source: newspec-c.
